nodal_ministry: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Govt of India
summary: Income support scheme providing Rs. 6,000 per year in three equal four-monthly installments of Rs. 2,000 each directly transferred to the bank accounts of eligible landholder farmer families.

eligibility.target_group: All landholding farmer families with cultivable landholding in their names.
exclusions: Farmer families holding constitutional posts (former or present)
Former and present Ministers, MPs, MLAs, MLCs, Mayors, Chairpersons of District Panchayats
Serving or retired officers and employees of Central/State Govt Ministries/Offices/PSUs/Autonomous bodies (excluding Multi Tasking Staff / Class IV / Group D employees)
All superannuated/retired pensioners with monthly pension of Rs. 10,000 or more
All persons who paid Income Tax in last assessment year
Professionals like Doctors, Engineers, Lawyers, Chartered Accountants, and Architects
documents_required: Bank Account details linked with Aadhaar

benefits: Rs. 6,000 per annum paid in 3 installments of Rs. 2,000 every 4 months (April-July, August-November, December-March) via DBT.
application_process: Farmers can register online at the PM-KISAN portal (pmkisan.gov.in) using 'Farmer Corner', or through Common Service Centres (CSCs) or State Nodal Officers.

nodal_ministry: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Govt of India
summary: Comprehensive crop insurance scheme providing financial support to farmers suffering crop loss/damage arising out of non-preventable natural risks from pre-sowing to post-harvest.

eligibility.target_group: All farmers growing notified crops in notified areas including sharecroppers and tenant farmers. Voluntary for all farmers.
exclusions: Crops not notified in the area by state government
Losses due to war, nuclear risks, malicious damage, theft, or domestic animals
documents_required: Land Record (Pahani / RTC / Land Possession Certificate)
Sowing certificate issued by Patwari / Village Agriculture Worker / Revenue officer
Bank Passbook copy linked to Aadhaar

benefits: Maximum premium payable by farmers is only 2% for all Kharif food & oilseeds crops, 1.5% for all Rabi food & oilseeds crops, and 5% for annual commercial/horticultural crops. The remaining premium is shared 50:50 by Central and State Governments.
application_process: Enrollment through National Crop Insurance Portal (pmfby.gov.in), authorized banks, or CSCs before cutoff date for Kharif (typically July 31) and Rabi (typically December 31).

nodal_ministry: Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance & MoA&FW
summary: Timely and hassle-free institutional short-term credit facility for farmers to meet cultivation expenses, post-harvest expenses, marketing loans, and working capital for maintenance of farm assets and allied activities (dairy, fisheries, poultry).

eligibility.target_group: Individual/joint farmers, owner cultivators, tenant farmers, oral lessees, sharecroppers, Self Help Groups (SHGs) or Joint Liability Groups (JLGs) of farmers.
exclusions: Defaulters with existing unregularized institutional agricultural loans
documents_required: ID Proof (Aadhaar / Voter ID / Driving License)

benefits: Credit limit up to Rs. 3 Lakh at an effective interest rate of 4% per annum (standard interest rate 9%, with 2% interest subvention by GoI and 3% prompt repayment incentive). Collateral-free loan up to Rs. 1.6 Lakh (extendable to Rs. 2 Lakh for tie-up arrangements).
application_process: Apply at any commercial bank, Regional Rural Bank (RRB), or Cooperative Bank branch, or online through state agri-credit portals.

nodal_ministry: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Govt of India
summary: Periodic assessment of farm soil fertility status across 12 parameters (Macro: N, P, K; Secondary: S; Micro: Zn, Fe, Cu, Mn, Bo; Physical: pH, EC, OC) along with customized dosage recommendations for crops.

eligibility.target_group: All farmers across all States and Union Territories in India.
documents_required: Survey number / plot identification of field sample

benefits: Free soil test report issued every 3 years providing exact nutrient deficiency analysis and crop-specific fertilizer and organic manure recommendations to reduce input costs and preserve soil health.
application_process: Soil samples collected by State Agriculture Department field officers and Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs). Farmers can download their card online using survey number at soilhealth.dac.gov.in.
